title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
summary: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

AI.tldr: ProTEUS是一种蛋白质进化模型，通过结合序列、进化和结构信息，高效预测突变效果，并利用实验反馈指导蛋白质进化。
AI.motivation: 蛋白质工程面临的问题是实验筛选难以覆盖巨大的序列空间，需要高效计算模型来指导蛋白质进化。
AI.method: ProTEUS使用MutationFormer架构学习序列、进化和结构信息的联合表示，并开发了快速的物理约束全原子预测器。
AI.result: ProTEUS在突变预测任务中表现优于现有模型，并在醛脱氢酶和左聚糖酶的实验中实现了10倍以上的活性提升。
AI.conclusion: ProTEUS提供了一种结合虚拟预测和实验反馈的高效蛋白质进化框架。

title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
comment: 34 pages, 19 figures (6 main text, 13 supplementary); code available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs
summary: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

AI.tldr: ANTIOCH-VS是一个开源框架，通过结合多种计算方法从蛋白质序列到候选配体的虚拟筛选，无需配体结合晶体结构即可高效识别结合态。
AI.motivation: 针对大多数靶标缺乏配体结合晶体结构的问题，开发一个自动化、全流程的虚拟筛选工具，提高筛选效率。
AI.method: 使用ColabFold构建构象集合，通过AlphaFold2-RAVE选择适合对接的构象，结合DOCK6或AutoDock Vina进行对接，并通过物理模拟优化结果。
AI.result: 在JAK2激酶和ADRB2 GPCR的测试中，ANTIOCH-VS表现出高效识别能力，命中率显著高于随机筛选。
AI.conclusion: ANTIOCH-VS为虚拟筛选提供了一种高效、自动化的解决方案，尤其适用于无配体结合结构的靶标。

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

AI.tldr: Bonbon是一个多模态生物学基础模型，通过无监督训练在大规模蛋白质-配体序列上表现出零样本的涌现能力，包括功能、残基和键级别的任务。
AI.motivation: 研究旨在探索大规模无监督训练在生物学中的潜力，验证基础模型能否在分子交互任务中展现涌现能力。
AI.method: Bonbon训练于3.2万亿个蛋白质-配体序列对，无需特定任务监督或结构坐标，通过六种规模的模型进行实验。
AI.result: 模型在最大规模下表现出涌现能力的显著跃升，且泛化能力强，湿实验室验证中61.5%的命中率表现优异。
AI.conclusion: 该研究表明参数/标记比是影响涌现能力的关键因素，同时展示了基础模型在生物药物发现中的潜力。
